verdict.rationale: Figma Make's docs describe an interactive app preview inside the Make file, plus a dedicated fullscreen preview. Users can annotate and draw on that preview to steer the agent while building, and publishing is a separate later step that deploys the app. missing for 10: explicit documentation that the preview updates live as changes are generated, independent or hands-on corroboration of the in-build preview experience.

support.subject: As a founder, I can interact with a live preview of my app while building, before publishing

citations.quote: Once you have your interactive app, you can also view it in [a dedicated, fullscreen preview]
Add [annotations](https://help.figma.com/hc/en-us/articles/42009840449175#h_01M30Q06FXE1CSX4XT91NBD0A4) to your Make preview to give the agent instructions for specific elements
mark up the preview and add those areas to your prompts
Publishing deploys your app and its Payload backend to Figma’s hosted infrastructure.
